research_question: RQ-N: do the near-zero shap_sum effect and the small select_shap effect survive when the source labels feeding the teacher and the downstream fit are partially corrupted, at graded noise levels below the full within-project permutation the permuted_original arm already tests?
status: FROZEN before execution. Any script implementing this analysis must reproduce the noise levels and injection rule exactly as specified below; any deviation must be disclosed, not silently corrected.
relationship_to_existing_arms: permuted_original (already run in v3) fully permutes each source project's labels within itself, preserving class counts but destroying every feature-label pairing (100% corrupted, in the sense that every label's pairing with its own row is broken). This sensitivity instead flips a small, graded FRACTION of labels, leaving the rest of the pairing intact, so it tests partial label-quality degradation rather than total signal destruction.
injection_rule: For a given noise level p and a given (seed, teacher) checkpoint: within each source project independently, select floor(p * n_project_rows) rows uniformly at random (without replacement) using a new 'labelnoise' random stream role, distinct from the existing 'labelperm' role used by permuted_original, and flip each selected row's label (0 becomes 1, 1 becomes 0). Target labels are never touched. This does not preserve per-project class counts (unlike permute_within_groups); it is a direct corruption, and the resulting class-count drift is reported, not corrected.
target_information_boundary: Identical to v3: target responses enter scoring only. This sensitivity only perturbs SOURCE labels.
arms_not_rerun: p_aug, ps_aug, pn_aug, pr_aug, coral, prevalence, permuted_original are out of scope for this sensitivity.
note_on_scope: The teacher is refit on the noisy source labels (so shap_sum/select_shap weights are themselves computed from corrupted labels, not just the downstream classifier), because the research question is whether the SHAP-derived signal survives label noise, not only whether a downstream classifier is robust to it.

grid.note: Everything else identical to protocol_v3.json, run once per noise level in noise_levels. Estimated cost: 3 noise levels x 6 arms, same 140-checkpoint grid as v3's main run per level -- comparable in scale to one capacity-sweep or teacher_grouped sensitivity run, not a full-factorial 13-arm rerun.

scored_against: true, unpolluted target labels (never the noisy source labels)
aggregation: Identical to v3: average repeats, teachers and learners within target, then equal-target mean. Leave-one-target-out aggregation sensitivity reported for both new comparisons at each noise level.

predeclared_thresholds.basis: Same v3 main-run figures used in protocol_decorrelation.json, fixed before this sensitivity is executed.
predeclared_thresholds.conclusion_robust_to_noise_level_p_if: mean_difference for shap_sum-vs-uniform_sum, shap_sum-vs-shuffled_sum and select_shap-vs-select_random at that noise level stays below 0.02 ROC-AUC in absolute value AND does not change sign relative to the noise-free v3 main-run value for the same comparison.
predeclared_thresholds.conclusion_flagged_as_noise_sensitive_at: any of the three comparisons at that level exceeds 0.02 ROC-AUC in absolute value, or changes sign.
predeclared_thresholds.absolute_performance_anchor: original-arm ROC-AUC at each noise level is also compared against the noise-free v3 original-arm baseline, to report how much noise alone degrades absolute performance independent of any weighting or selection effect.

what_this_would_show: If the small effects are stable across all three noise levels, the v3 conclusion is not an artefact of assuming clean labels. If a comparison degrades or reverses at a noise level well below the full permutation already shown to destroy signal (permuted_original), that specifies how much label-quality erosion the reported effects can tolerate before becoming unreliable, which is a concrete, checkable claim the current manuscript does not make.
inference: Descriptive fixed-benchmark effect, matching v3. No significance test, confidence interval or equivalence bound. Target rotations share source projects.
